title: Layout in Compose: Column, Row, Box, constraints and modifiers

videos.script: A screen in Compose is boxes inside boxes. This lesson is about who decides how big each box is, and where it goes. {{containers}} Three containers do almost all of it. A Column stacks things down, a Row lays them across, and a Box puts one on top of another. You will build the planner's session row and a course card with a badge. {{order}} Then modifiers. They look like settings, and they are not. They are a chain, and swapping two of them gives you a different drawing. {{constraints}} Then the part most people never see. Every parent tells each child the smallest and largest it may be. The child picks a size, and the parent places it. A test prints that whole conversation, number by number. {{weight}} That printout explains weight. A weighted child is measured last, and gets only what is left. {{layout}} And when no container says what you mean, you write the conversation yourself. Ten lines of code, and the planner gets a bar for the week.
